sourceInformation.genre: Action: third-person crime action with dialogue chapters
sourceInformation.perspective: Third-person by default (threequarter view); the Camera key (V, or pad R3) also turns it to top-down and isometric
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge 0.85.1 (single-file 2D engine, procedural pixels, Canvas 2D, Web Audio); AI Hub client aihub-session 1.3.0 (protocol 1); no other dependencies
sourceInformation.artDirection: Engine-native pixel look (PS1 style, 320x240 internal resolution), dusk palette with neon signs and a North Jersey skyline
sourceInformation.animation: The engine's procedural Humanoid rig with its move set (jab, cross, haymaker, overhead)
sourceInformation.audio: All made in code: four music tracks, sound effects, and Animalese (a blip per letter, each at its own pitch). No recorded voices or sound files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub session, parallel mode, 1 to 4 players; a three-minute round scored on cash, respect, kills and calm
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium via Playwright (desktop and a phone profile); the AI Hub harness with two players and a 40-second round
sourceInformation.research: Read the engine's agent guide and API header and the AI Hub session protocol; no web searches
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux; browser unknown

testingFeedback: Issues found: 11. Seven came from the test runs; four came from reading the map, the code and the screenshots.

Critical or game-breaking: 2. The attract demo's own button taps counted as player input, so it left every talk half done; and a spawn point sat in the pool water, a blocked cell, where the finale's boss would have stood.
Most helpful test: the attract run with a state log every tenth of a second. It showed the stalls, the bot stuck on a wall, and the demo leaving after a win.
Least helpful test: the random key fuzz. It found no exceptions, but it cannot say whether the game is right.
engineFeedback: Most liked: the Story module (conversations as data, flags, quests, state for a save), and the standard pause, settings, glyphs and corner menu.

Stuck or guessed wrong: the settings' 'saved' flag is true before anything is stored, so a 'set only if none saved' check never runs. The engine also has no stick invert pair, only the aim's, and music names must be registered before use.
Most important thing I built: the town layout, the crew's sight and chase, the chapters and their objectives, and the Animalese hook per letter.
Hardest part: a 1.2 MB single file of 14,706 lines; the API had to be read from the source comments and the agent header.
To remove or overhaul: the settings' 'saved' flag. Name it for what it is, or default it to false.
To change: an input preset that merges with a base, so a game adds one action without copying the whole table.
promptFeedback: Most liked: the controller-first rules, the hub protocol link, and the exit-interview shape, which made the done line checkable.
Confusing: the bracketed file names and the template title; the Testing questions, which could mean either the test plan or its results; and whether a hub round needs its own score.
Hardest: fitting the attract mode, the hub round and the full engine's menus into one build without any of them breaking the others.
One test to add: a scripted play-through that uses real inputs for every chapter, plus a pad emulation for the invert toggles and the glyphs.

aiHub.name: Sopranos Sundays
aiHub.tagline: a Sunday in North Jersey, for the family
aiHub.description: Collect the envelopes, settle with Frankie's crew, and get through Sunday dinner in a third-person crime action game. Chapters, dialogue, and a three-minute parallel round for up to four players.
aiHub.controls: Stick or WASD move, J melee, G pistol, E talk, L dodge, K guard, C sneak, V camera
